BREAKING: Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted +$17.9 billion in inflows in August, the 2nd-largest monthly intake on record.

This pushed global gold ETF holdings up +121 tonnes, to a record 4,189 tonnes.

At the same time, total assets under management rose +16% MoM, to $615 billion, their highest level since February.

Europe led last month’s purchases at +$7.9 billion, its biggest monthly inflow on record, followed by North America at +$7.7 billion, and Asia at +$2 billion.

Within Europe, the UK posted +$4.4 billion in inflows, its 2nd-largest monthly inflow on record, followed by France at +$1.5 billion, its biggest monthly intake on record.

Year-to-date, global gold ETFs have attracted +$29 billion in inflows, equivalent to a +160 tonne increase in gold holdings.

Gold demand is remarkably strong.

items.content:
Investors are increasingly bearish on inflation-protected Treasuries:

Short interest on the TIPS ETF,  $TIP , is up to ~6% of shares outstanding, triple the levels seen in late 2025.

The fund tracks an index of inflation-protected Treasury bonds, whose prices generally fall when real yields rise.

This figure is now in-line with the highest levels recorded in December 2021, just 3 months before the Fed started hiking rates.

Short interest on  $TIP peaked at ~8% in Q2 but has remained above 4% for the majority of the year.

Investors are more aggressively betting against  $TIP prices as strong economic growth, rising fiscal concerns, and debt-fueled AI infrastructure investment have led investors to demand higher yields on Treasuries.

Real Treasury yields are gaining momentum.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Sep 10, 2026

items.title: Global food inflation is rapidly rising. The Bloomberg Agriculture Spot Index, which tracks 10 key agricultural commodities, soared over +13.0% in August, its largest monthly gain since July 2012. Meanwhile, the World Food Price Index rose +1.9% in August, to its highest since December 2022. This index tracks internationally traded staples including grains, sugar, dairy, meat, and vegetable oils. Food prices have risen +7.4% since January. Every component tracked in the index rose last month, led by a +11.9% increase in sugar prices and a +2.6% gain in wheat prices. Wheat prices have now increased +15.0% over the last 12 months. Global food inflation is heating up.

As we wrote in our below post yesterday, we are on track to see 5.00%+ by next week.

As a result, borrowing costs skyrocketing for both the US government and US consumers.

Now, the housing market is effectively frozen and US homebuyers are walking away from deals at the highest rate since 2023.

The bond market is quite literally fighting the US Treasury.

Prepare for a highly eventful Q4.The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter)You can't make this up.

The US Treasury just announced it is tripling long-term buybacks to $6 billion and yields STILL rallied on the news.

That means the US Treasury went from doubling, to "at least doubling," to tripling long-term bond buybacks and yields are still rising.

This puts the 10Y Note Yield above 4.85% for the first time since November 2023, up +15 basis points from pre-announcement levels.

The bond market is quite literally fighting the US Treasury as the Iran War continues, with the 10Y Note Yield nearing a +100 basis point move since the war began.

Without an end to the Iran War, we are on track to see the 10Y Note Yield above 5.00% by next week.

American consumers, homebuyers, and borrowers are in for a rude awakening.—  https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2097719382533177507
